steps.name: Consolidated TF activity report
caveats: Ranking stability at n=6 per group is limited; small differences in rank between adjacent TFs are not meaningful
steps.context: Six per group is a workable but modest design: it supports a ranked hypothesis list, not a claim that a named TF drives the phenotype. The report must not overstate that.
steps.question: Which transcription factors are the best-supported candidate drivers of the aldosterone response in these kidney samples, and how confident can that claim be at 6 samples per group?

grounding.reason: Activity report states network, version, statistic, estimator, min regulon size, regulator count and the inference caution (R-0119), with the full reproducibility record (R-0086).

constraints: Do not present a TF activity score as evidence that the TF is differentially expressed, or the reverse

steps.description: Assemble the results of T1S1, T1S2, T2S1, T2S2 and T2S3 into one report. Lead with the ranked TF answer and the strength of evidence for it. plan.title: Aldosterone vs vehicle kidney: TF activity inference
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question asks which transcription factors drive the aldosterone-treated kidney samples relative to vehicle controls. The input is a single raw Salmon gene-level count matrix (counts.csv, 12,000 genes x 12 samples, gene symbols in the first column) with a 12-row metadata table carrying one condition column; the design is 6 aldosterone vs 6 vehicle, unpaired, single batch. TF activity cannot be measured — it is inferred from a prior TF-target network — so the plan builds the two inputs that inference needs and then runs it twice, on two networks, so the report can state overlap and disagreement rather than a single ranked list.

T1S1 does sample-structure QC on blind-VST values (PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) so an outlier or a depth artefact is visible before any inference. T1S2 fits the gene-level model: minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size), DESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization inside the model, design ~condition with the vehicle/control level set explicitly as reference, Wald test for aldosterone vs vehicle, apeglm shrinkage for reporting, BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering on. Its purpose here is not the gene list per se but the per-gene Wald statistic that the contrast-level TF inference consumes, plus the log2-CPM matrix for the per-sample inference.

T2S1 is the core step: decoupleR univariate linear model on the CollecTRI human regulons, signed edges kept so a repressor target lowers the score, minimum regulon size 5. It runs in both modes the question needs — one score per sample from the log2-CPM matrix, tested between the two conditions with limma and BH across regulators, and one score per regulator from the full vector of Wald statistics of every tested gene (never a thresholded list). T2S2 repeats the inference on DoRothEA confidence A-C as a second network and reports the overlap and disagreement of the top regulators; a TF that is top-ranked under only one network is flagged as network-dependent. T2S3 adds PROGENy pathway footprints (mlm) as upstream context for the TF calls — aldosterone acts through the mineralocorticoid receptor NR3C2, so a coherent story would place the top TFs downstream of an identifiable signalling footprint.

Two hard constraints run through the plan. First, with 6 per group and 12 samples total, a regulatory network cannot be inferred from this expression matrix — ARACNe-style mutual information needs on the order of a hundred samples — so every regulon comes from prior knowledge, and the report must say that a prior network is tissue-agnostic: a kidney-specific regulator can be missed and a target silent in kidney adds noise. Second, an activity score is an inference, not a measurement; the top TFs are hypotheses for follow-up. Both CollecTRI (human, v2.0) and DoRothEA (human) are present in the reference store, matching the human organism of the data. T3S1 assembles the report with the required provenance fields.

steps.method: Sample structure QC: blind VST, PCA on top-variance genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes
Pre-filter: at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples
DESeq2 design ~condition with control as reference level
DESeq2 Wald test, aldosterone vs vehicle
apeglm shrinkage of the condition coefficient
decoupleR ulm on the CollecTRI regulons, per-sample log2 CPM scores plus contrast on the Wald statistic
decoupleR ulm on DoRothEA confidence A-C regulons as a robustness check
decoupleR mlm on the PROGENy footprint model
Activity report with network name and version, input statistic, contrast, estimator, min regulon size, n regulators tested, inference caution, plus reproducibility record

A TF significant under only one network is network-dependent and must be labelled as such.
steps.context: Two curated networks disagree because their curation differs, not because one is wrong. The purpose is to separate TF calls that are robust to the choice of prior from those that are an artefact of it — with 6 samples per group this distinction carries more weight than the ranking itself.
acceptance_criteria: Ranked TF table from the second network with score, p-value and BH-adjusted p-value, and the confidence levels retained stated
Overlap of top regulators between the two networks quantified, plus rank correlation over the shared TFs
Explicit list of TFs significant under one network only, labelled network-dependent
Number of regulators tested under each network reported side by side
constraints: Keep only the higher-confidence interactions (levels A to C) and state the levels used
Use the HUMAN collection — do not use the mouse regulon file present in the same store
Keep the mode of regulation sign; minimum regulon size 5; identical estimator and inputs to T2S1 so the comparison isolates the network

If the second human network is absent from the reference store at run time, report that the robustness check could not be run and leave the T2S1 result standing with that caveat stated — do not substitute an unsigned target set as if it were a signed regulon
caveats: Overlap between the two networks is itself partly a curation artefact — shared literature sources inflate agreement, so concordance is weaker evidence than it appears
An unsigned ChIP-binding target collection is not an alternative here: binding is not regulation and carries no direction

grounding.reason: DoRothEA confidence A-C is the named alternative regulon set (R-0113); when two networks run, the report gives overlap and disagreement of the top regulators (R-0119).

steps.name: PROGENy pathway footprints as upstream context
steps.question: Which signalling pathway footprints differ between aldosterone-treated and vehicle kidney samples, and are they consistent with the transcription factors called in T2S1?
steps.description: Run decoupleR's multivariate linear model (mlm) on the PROGENy human footprint model using the top 500 responsive genes per pathway, scoring both the per-sample log2-CPM matrix (tested aldosterone vs vehicle with limma, BH across pathways) and the contrast-level Wald statistic vector from T1S2. Report pathway scores beside the TF results and state whether the leading footprints are consistent with the top-ranked regulators. Confirm the PROGENy model is available in the environment (via the decoupleR/OmniPath resources or the reference store) before running; if it is not, report that this contextual step could not run and continue — the TF answer in T2S1 and T2S2 does not depend on it.
steps.context: Aldosterone acts through the mineralocorticoid receptor; a pathway footprint that moves coherently with the top TFs strengthens the mechanistic reading, and one that does not is a flag that the TF ranking may be driven by a few high-weight targets.
acceptance_criteria: Pathway activity table with score, p-value and BH-adjusted p-value per pathway for the aldosterone vs vehicle contrast
Per-sample pathway score matrix across the 12 samples
Written comparison of the leading pathway footprints against the top TFs from T2S1
Statement of the number of responsive genes per pathway used and how many were present in the matrix
constraints: Use the human PROGENy model; top 500 responsive genes per pathway
Read a score as a transcriptional footprint of the pathway, not as expression of its member genes
BH adjustment across pathways
This step is contextual: if the footprint model is unavailable, report the absence and do not substitute a membership-based pathway enrichment presented as an activity
caveats: A footprint model carries no pathway topology — SPIA, the tool of record for topology-aware pathway impact, is absent from this environment and the report must say the result uses no graph structure
A pathway member can change expression without a change in pathway activity and the reverse

grounding.reason: Pathway activity as upstream context: PROGENy footprints with decoupleR mlm on the top 500 responsive genes (R-0115); SPIA absent, so no topology is used and the report states it (R-0122).

steps.name: Consolidated TF activity report
steps.question: Which transcription factors are the best-supported candidate drivers of the aldosterone response in these kidney samples, and how confident can that claim be at 6 samples per group?
steps.description: Assemble the results of T1S1, T1S2, T2S1, T2S2 and T2S3 into one report. Lead with the ranked TF answer and the strength of evidence for it. For every activity result state: the network name and version, the input statistic and the contrast (condition, aldosterone, vehicle), the estimator, the minimum regulon size, and the number of regulators that entered the test. State plainly that an activity score is an inference from a prior knowledge network and not a measurement, so a high-scoring TF is a hypothesis for experimental follow-up. Mark every TF that only one of the two networks called. Include the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, any random seed used, and the version of each regulon and footprint collection consumed. Include the QC verdict from T1S1 and the count of genes passing padj < 0.05 from T1S2 as the context in which the TF ranking should be read.
steps.context: Six per group is a workable but modest design: it supports a ranked hypothesis list, not a claim that a named TF drives the phenotype. The report must not overstate that.
acceptance_criteria: Ranked candidate TF list leading the report, with the network(s) supporting each and the BH-adjusted p-value
All required activity provenance fields present: network name and version, input statistic, contrast, estimator, minimum regulon size, number of regulators tested
Explicit inference caution stating that activity is inferred from a prior network and is tissue-agnostic
Network-dependent TF calls flagged individually
Reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, seeds, and collection versions
Any step that could not run because a reference was unavailable is named, with what was lost
constraints: Do not present a TF activity score as evidence that the TF is differentially expressed, or the reverse
Do not report a TF as a driver on the strength of one network alone without labelling it network-dependent
State the sample size (6 aldosterone vs 6 vehicle) wherever a confidence claim is made
caveats: Ranking stability at n=6 per group is limited; small differences in rank between adjacent TFs are not meaningful

grounding.reason: Activity report states network, version, statistic, estimator, min regulon size, regulator count and the inference caution (R-0119), with the full reproducibility record (R-0086).
